title: Universal link between structural relaxation and self-diffusion in simple supercooled liquids
authors: Mingyu Zhu, Xinyu Chang, Licun Fu, Yiming Zheng, Lijin Wang
abstract: arXiv:2610.22385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite a vigorous effort, a comprehensive and satisfactory understanding of the dynamics underlying the glass transition in finite-dimensional systems has not yet emerged. One key hallmark of supercooled liquids approaching the glass transition is the breakdown of the classical Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, manifested as the decoupling between the self-diffusion coefficient and structural relaxation time, commonly described by a fractional SE relation. Whether and how the fractional SE exponents vary remains an ongoing debate, even for the simplest supercooled liquids. In this work, we numerically establish a universal relation between the self-diffusion coefficient and structural relaxation time by introducing characteristic scales that are revealed under the condition of constant dynamical heterogeneity. Moreover, this universal relation could also capture literature data for supercooled water and silica. Remarkably, we find that the fractional SE exponent is invariant across various supercooled liquids studied spanning a wide range of fragility, thereby challenging the prevailing view that the fractional SE exponent is correlated with fragility. Our study demonstrates that investigating dynamical heterogeneity yields more valuable insights into understanding glassy dynamics than expected.
summary:
- Universal scaling links self‑diffusion and structural relaxation time at constant dynamical heterogeneity.
- Fractional Stokes‑Einstein exponent is invariant across liquids of different fragility.
- Scaling reproduces data for supercooled water and silica, underscoring dynamical heterogeneity’s central role.

title: Noise-Induced Restoration of Entropy Concavity Near Gaussian Equilibrium
abstract: arXiv:2610.22386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quantitative form of noise-induced restoration of entropy concavity for one-dimensional nonequilibrium states relaxing toward a Gaussian thermal equilibrium. A partially thermalized state is modeled by $X_q=\sqrt q\,X+\sqrt{1-q}\,G$, where $G$ is Gaussian equilibrium noise and $q$ is the retained signal fraction. For two independently prepared copies we ask when the entropy of the mixed state $h(\sqrt{1-t}\,X_q+\sqrt t\,Y_q)$ is concave in the mixing parameter. The problem is motivated by entropy geometry along Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/Fokker--Planck relaxation, where the relative score is the nonequilibrium thermodynamic force and relative Fisher information is entropy-production rate. We derive an exact symmetric endpoint-curvature formula, separating a nonnegative Ornstein--Uhlenbeck restoring term from a fourth-cumulant correction, and extend it to nonsmooth generalized-Gaussian states $e^{-a|x|^p}$ for $p>3/2$. For half thermalization of a symmetric log-concave input, posterior-variance identities give a quantitative outer-region theorem confining any endpoint obstruction to two explicitly bounded near-equilibrium sectors. We also give spectral and MMSE reformulations of the auxiliary inequality $A\ge2\delta$, prove it in an explicit nonlinear neighborhood of Gaussian equilibrium, and show how it sharpens the endpoint bounds. The main all-mixing result concerns the leading symmetric non-Gaussian Hermite mode: for $p_a=\phiG(1+a\He_4)$, $0<a><1$ and every $0<q><q\le4/7$ for this explicit nonequilibrium family. Numerical searches over broader log-concave families are reported only as supporting evidence.
summary:
- Demonstrates that adding Gaussian noise restores concavity of entropy for partially thermalized one‑dimensional states, deriving an exact endpoint‑curvature formula separating OU‑restoring and fourth‑cumulant terms.
- Extends the result to nonsmooth generalized‑Gaussian densities \(e^{-a|x|^p}\) (\(p>3/2\)) and proves an outer‑region theorem bounding endpoint obstructions to two near‑equilibrium sectors.
- Provides spectral and MMSE reformulations of the key inequality \(A\ge2\delta\), proving it near Gaussian equilibrium and sharpening bounds for the leading non‑Gaussian Hermite mode.

title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians
abstract: arXiv:2610.22387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians. The latest release v0.4.0 holds 1434 energies on 395 instances of six model families and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 153 have no exact solution and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.
summary:
- Introduces QMBL, an interactive leaderboard cataloging published ground‑state energies for lattice Hamiltonians.
- Current release v0 lists 1,434 energies across 395 instances of six model families, with 153 unsolved cases.
- Serves as a consensus layer for variational results and a target list for the companion benchmark “QMBL: Open Problems.”

title: Thermodynamics of coupled electromagnetic and mass fields
abstract: arXiv:2610.22391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a unified thermodynamic framework for chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport by extending the Gibbs--Duhem relation to include kinetic free-energy contributions associated with material and field motion. The resulting kinetic Gibbs--Duhem relation establishes a thermodynamic connection between free-energy variations, generalized chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum, while preserving the invariance of the system free energy under changes of reference frame. Within a Lagrangian formulation of free-energy evolution, the relation provides a common structure for diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics. For nonuniform chemical systems, the framework recovers the coupling between Cahn--Hilliard dynamics and the Korteweg stress arising from composition gradients. Its extension to electromagnetic systems incorporates electric, magnetic, charge, and mechanical contributions into the same thermodynamic formulation, yielding a unified description of electromagnetic and momentum evolution. The framework further separates dissipative from nondissipative transport and establishes a common thermodynamic form for mechanical and electromagnetic propagation. In the isentropic limit, the characteristic propagation velocity is determined by the derivative of the thermodynamic pressure with respect to density, yielding the speed of sound for mechanical systems and the speed of light for electromagnetic systems. These results show that kinetic contributions can be incorporated consistently into the Gibbs--Duhem framework, providing a common thermodynamic basis for coupled chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport without introducing separate thermodynamic principles for each mechanism.
summary:
- Unified Gibbs–Duhem relation incorporating kinetic free‑energy links free‑energy, chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum.
- Lagrangian framework unifies diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics, reproducing Cahn–Hilliard/Korteweg coupling.
- Distinguishes dissipative vs nondissipative transport; isentropic propagation speed follows from pressure‑density derivative, yielding sound and light speeds.

title: Visualizing surface-reaction-driven chloride migration and cascading failure in sulfide solid electrolytes
authors: Xiaoya He, Haoran Zhang, Xinyang Yue, Hang Liu, Zian Mao, Jialong Wang, Min Liu, Shufen Chu, Liwei Chen, Zhaoxin Yu, Xi Liu, Chuying Ouyang, Ziyang Ning, Yujun Xie
abstract: arXiv:2610.22394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moisture instability of sulfide solid electrolytes limits practical use in all-solid-state batteries. Spatially resolving gas--solid reactions during moisture exposure remains challenging. Here, cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (cryo-4D-STEM) maps nanoscale degradation in low- and high-Cl argyrodite electrolytes, Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl and Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\). Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl undergoes predominantly surface-localized degradation that progressively extends inward, whereas Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\) exhibits rapid interior amorphization accompanied by outward chloride redistribution. Density functional theory calculations indicate a lower chloride-migration barrier along the modeled pathway in the higher-Cl composition, while chloride removal and vacancy formation distort the PS\(_4^{3-}\) framework and may destabilize the lattice. Surface treatment suppresses detectable large-scale chloride segregation and improves moisture tolerance, retaining 99.9% of the capacity measured at the start of 0.33 C cycling after 150 cycles. These results identify chloride redistribution as a key process in degradation propagation and suggest a route toward moisture-tolerant solid-state batteries.
summary:
- Cryo‑4D‑STEM shows Li₆PS₅Cl degrades mainly at the surface, while Li₅.₅PS₄.₅Cl₁.₅ undergoes rapid interior amorphization and outward Cl redistribution.
- DFT indicates a lower Cl‑migration barrier in the high‑Cl electrolyte; Cl removal creates vacancies that distort the PS₄ framework, destabilizing the lattice.
- Surface treatment suppresses Cl segregation, improving moisture tolerance and retaining 9 % of initial capacity after 150 cycles at 33 C.

title: Synergistic Self-Driven Nanoconfinement and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Deeply Supercooled "No Man's Land" Water
abstract: arXiv:2610.22402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The 150--235 K ``no man's land'' (NML) of deeply supercooled water is a highly debated regime where rapid crystallization hinders experimental observation of the hypothesized liquid-liquid phase transition. Using TIP4P/2005 molecular dynamics simulations, we uncover a structurally and dynamically heterogeneous state at ambient pressure that exhibits novel physical features. Our results demonstrate that this low-density state ($\rho \approx 0.925$ g/cm$^3$) is a unique supercooled liquid, distinct from both glassy and spinodal states. Specifically, it emerges as a stable, structurally arrested phase driven by a self-generated ``soft skeleton'' of nanoclusters. This network forms an intrinsic nanoporous structure that imposes nanoconfinement on the remaining fluid, proving that NML confinement can be an entirely self-driven phenomenon. Finally, we resolve the temperature-dependent, nonlinear behavior of density and compressibility, highlighting a structurally driven anomaly that clarifies the thermodynamics of deep supercooling. Collectively, this work provides a transformative structural framework for understanding the anomalous nature of water within the NML.
summary:
- Self‑generated nanocluster “soft skeleton” creates intrinsic nanoporous confinement in deeply supercooled water (150–235 K).
- Low‑density (~925 g cm⁻³) phase is a distinct, stable liquid with pronounced structural and dynamical heterogeneity, separate from glass or spinodal states.
- Nonlinear temperature dependence of density and compressibility is explained as a structurally driven anomaly, clarifying water’s thermodynamics in the “no‑man's land”.

title: Semiclassical Analysis of Wave Dynamics via Wigner Transforms: Applications to the Quantum Harmonic, Anharmonic, and Dirac Oscillator
abstract: arXiv:2610.22414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this Master's thesis, we give a pedagogical introduction to the semiclassical analysis of wave dynamics in single-band and multi-band systems. We show how the semiclassical evolutions of Wigner functions can approximate the dynamics of wave packet centers and wave packet deformations. Three systems of increasing complexity are considered: the quantum harmonic oscillator and the quantum anharmonic oscillator as single-band systems, and the Dirac oscillator as a two-band system. We explain the origins of the first-order semiclassical corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn-Flynn, and Berry) in the equations of motion and examine their effects on predictive accuracy. Another focus is set on the conditions for validity of the semiclassical analysis. For both the quantum anharmonic and the Dirac oscillators, a dimensionless parameter controlling the accuracy of the approximation is identified. In multi-band systems, the formalism applies only to states within a single adiabatic subspace, which, for the Dirac oscillator, corresponds to an energy branch. This motivates the construction of single-branch almost coherent states: approximately Gaussian wave packets formed by superpositions of states from a single energy branch. Their centers undergo oscillations with an aperiodic envelope. These states enable comparison between semiclassical Wigner function evolution and the commonly used Sundaram-Niu formalism. We show that semiclassical Wigner function evolution captures deformation-related dynamics, including the initial decay of oscillations, which the Sundaram-Niu formalism cannot describe by construction. Additionally, exact quantum evolution reveals partial relocalization of these single-branch almost coherent states, a phenomenon that cannot be captured by the semiclassical evolution.
summary:
- Semiclassical Wigner‑function dynamics for single‑band (harmonic, anharmonic) and two‑band (Dirac) oscillators.
- First‑order corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn‑Flynn, Berry) and a dimensionless accuracy parameter for anharmonic and Dirac cases.
- Construction of single‑branch almost coherent states to compare Wigner evolution with the Sundaram‑Niu formalism.

title: Probing nonequilibrium transport and density profiles in tilted interacting fermion chains with local reservoirs
authors: Andrea Nava, N. Aucar Boidi, Reinhold Egger, Karen Hallberg, C. R. Proetto
abstract: arXiv:2610.22463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how local particle reservoirs can probe transport and density profiles in tilted spinless fermion chains with nearest-neighbor interactions. Using finite-chain Lindblad calculations with particle injection and extraction at opposite ends, we define a threshold-dependent transmission range from the stationary current as the chain length is varied. This range decreases with increasing tilt and follows the trends of the equilibrium density-crossover width in the parameter regimes studied. Interactions can enhance transmission by compensating field-induced energy costs, whereas strongly polarized configurations suppress transport. A third, weakly coupled extraction reservoir provides a complementary spatial probe: its current is exactly proportional to the local occupation in the presence of the probe, and the normalized current approaches the unperturbed nonequilibrium density as the probe coupling vanishes. We illustrate the detection of staggered density modulations and show that bulk densities can continue to relax after boundary currents have nearly stabilized. These protocols connect current measurements to spatial transmission and density structure in driven interacting chains.
summary:
- Local particle reservoirs in a tilted, interacting fermion chain reveal transport and density profiles via Lindblad dynamics.
- Transmission range narrows with increasing tilt; interactions can either compensate field‑induced energy costs or suppress transport in polarized regimes.
- A weakly coupled extraction probe yields a current directly proportional to local occupation, enabling detection of staggered density modulations and bulk relaxation.

title: Anyon bound states in MoTe$_2$ Fractional Chern Insulators
abstract: arXiv:2610.22473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binding anyons to optically active excitons offers a route to manipulate fractional excitations and reveal the internal spatial structure of anyons. We establish the formation of anyon bound states between a mobile dipolar exciton and an $e/3$ quasihole in a twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$ fractional Chern insulator. Using exact diagonalization of a continuum-based interacting model, we identify a regime of meV-scale binding and strong exciton-quasihole entanglement controlled by exciton mobility and the distance between the exciton and the FCI. Spatial correlations resolve a localized depletion core carrying approximately $e/3$ charge around the exciton, providing a real-space characterization of the bound state. Beyond its fractional charge, the quasihole exhibits a moir\'e-induced octupolar structure. Interlayer tunneling anisotropy strongly deforms this structure while leaving the enclosed charge nearly unchanged, linking the internal profile of the anyon to the underlying electronic quantum geometry. These findings establish conditions for robust exciton-anyon binding in moir\'e heterostructures and show how these composites provide access to properties of fractional excitations beyond their total charge.
summary:
- Anyon–exciton bound states form between a mobile dipolar exciton and an \(e/3\) quasihole in twisted bilayer MoTe\(_2\) fractional Chern insulators.
- MeV‑scale binding and strong exciton–quasihole entanglement arise from exciton mobility and interlayer distance, with spatial correlations revealing a localized \(e/3\) depletion core and a moiré‑induced octupolar charge distribution.
- Interlayer tunneling anisotropy deforms the internal octupolar profile while preserving the total charge, linking the anyon’s internal structure to the underlying electronic quantum geometry.

title: Fractional Chern insulators and composite Fermi liquids vs. charge order in twisted MoTe$_2$
abstract: arXiv:2610.22479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The bandstructure of twisted MoTe$_2$ around 3.7$^\circ$ consists of spin-valley locked Chern bands with a bandwidth that is smaller than the interaction scale. As such, the strongly correlated phases familiar from Landau levels can be realized: Quantum Hall states, composite Fermi liquids and charge order. These states have in common that they are all favoured by strong interactions, however changing the quantum geometry and topology of the bands as well as their bandwidth via the displacement field and twist angle tilts the balance between them. We provide a comprehensive exact diagonalization analysis of the competition between these states and in particular elucidate the nature of the charge order at fillings $\nu=-\frac14,-\frac13,-\frac12,-\frac23$. Furthermore, we analyze the effect of band mixing by going beyond a single band per valley. This effect of band mixing is crucial for reconciling the numerical phase diagrams with experimental observations.
summary:
- Twisted MoTe₂ at ~7° hosts spin‑valley‑locked Chern bands with bandwidth < interaction scale, enabling Landau‑level‑like phases (QH, composite Fermi liquid, charge order).
- Exact diagonalization reveals charge‑ordered states at ν = −¼, −⅓, −½, −⅔, tunable by displacement field and twist angle.
- Band‑mixing beyond a single valley band is crucial to reconcile numerical phase diagrams with experimental observations.

title: Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators
authors: Fabian Pichler, Clemens Kuhlenkamp, Ashvin Vishwanath, Michael Knap
abstract: arXiv:2610.22498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. Yet the microscopic relation between them remains poorly understood. Here, we use tensor network simulations to study repulsively interacting spinless fermions in a tunable topological band of the checkerboard lattice. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. Surprisingly, a weak-coupling approach starting from a metallic parent state captures the nature of both ordered phases at intermediate coupling. We find that fluctuations in the metal generate longer-range attraction, which we analyze within the random-phase approximation. This approach captures the pairing symmetry as well as the radial form factors of the Cooper pairs, and incorporating this attraction into Hartree-Fock selects the observed Hall crystal. Together, these results identify fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient of ordering, while our tensor network computations establish the direct competition of both phases with FCIs.
summary:
- Tensor‑network study of repulsive spinless fermions on a checkerboard Chern band uncovers competing FCIs, chiral p‑wave superconductivity, and a Hall crystal.
- Enhancing band dispersion turns Jain‑sequence FCIs into chiral SC on both sides of half filling; at half filling strong coupling yields a doubled‑unit‑cell Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance.
- Weak‑coupling RPA shows metallic fluctuations generate long‑range attraction, reproducing the SC pairing symmetry and selecting the Hall crystal via Hartree‑Fock.

title: Bulk-Defect Correspondence in Algebraic Classical Spin Liquids
abstract: arXiv:2610.22585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local constraints in algebraic classical spin liquids give rise to singular momentum-space correlations. This so called pinch-point singularity carries a momentum-space winding number that determines the low-energy structure of the algebraic spin liquid. We show that nonmagnetic vacancies in two dimensions reveal this topological invariant in the real-space winding of the surrounding spin textures. Under explicit conditions, we prove this bulk-defect correspondence for rank-$n$ $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquids and verify it numerically for the Coulomb spin liquids of the kagome and checkerboard lattices and the rank-2 $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquid of the honeycomb-snowflake model. In this way we show that vacancies can be used as general probes for distinguishing the emergent gauge theories of strongly correlated classical disordered magnets.
summary:
- Pinch‑point singularities in momentum space carry a winding number that fixes the low‑energy structure of algebraic spin liquids.
- Nonmagnetic vacancies in 2D expose this invariant through real‑space winding of surrounding spin textures, proving a bulk‑defect correspondence.
- The correspondence is shown for rank‑\(n\) U(spin liquids and verified numerically on kagome, checkerboard, and honeycomb‑snowflake lattices, allowing vacancy probes of emergent gauge theories.

title: Coexistence of Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like behavior in La-doped antiferromagnetic CaMnO3
authors: Koustav Pal, Shuvendu Ghosh, N. N. S. V. Rama Raju, Chitrada Prasad, Kalipada Das, I. Das
abstract: arXiv:2610.22844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coexistence of a Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like short range interaction in a single-phase homogeneous manganite is of particular interest because it reveals multiple levels of magnetic clustering generated by disorder and competing exchange interactions. In bulk $\mathrm{La}_{0.19}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.81}\mathrm{MnO}_{3}$, this unusual magnetic state develops in the antiferromagnetic regime, where A-site disorder strongly modifies the local magnetic landscape. Rietveld analysis confirms a single-phase orthorhombic structure, while magnetic measurements establish a Griffiths phase below $T_{\mathrm{G}} = 280\text{ K}$ through the deviation from Curie-Weiss behavior. Superparamagnetic-like behavior persisting from 280 to 370 K further indicates that isolated magnetic clusters remain stable well into the nominally paramagnetic region. The presence of both phenomena highlights the crucial role of disorder-induced exchange randomness in stabilizing complex magnetic states in correlated perovskite oxides.
summary:
- La₀.₁₉Ca₀.₈₁MnO₃ is a single‑phase orthorhombic manganite exhibiting a Griffiths phase below 280 K and superparamagnetic‑like clusters up to 370 K.
- A‑site disorder creates exchange randomness that stabilizes magnetic clustering within the antiferromagnetic regime.
- Curie‑Weiss deviation below 280 K signals the Griffiths singularity, while persistent clusters above T_N reveal a complex, disorder‑driven magnetic state.

title: Kitaev, semi-Dirac, and spinon quantum spin Hall liquids on the square-hexagon-dodecagon lattice: A parent projective symmetry group classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.22965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The square-hexagon-dodecagon (SHD) lattice hosts an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid, while further-neighbor couplings frustrate its Heisenberg magnet into classically degenerate lines where quantum fluctuations can melt the N\'eel order. To place this state among the lattice's spin liquids, we classify fermionic parton mean-field states with singlet and spin-orbit-coupled triplet amplitudes by their projective symmetry groups (PSGs). As SHD sites lack site symmetry, its $Z_2$ PSGs are the projective classes of $p6mm$ with time reversal, from which those of every single-orbit $p6mm$ lattice follow. In the idealized Kitaev model, where lattice operations do not rotate spins, these liquids carry a single $Z_2$ PSG descending from the $SU(2)$ Lieb-flux state, and their projections are exact eigenstates. The PSG's sixfold-rotation sign, fixed by the dodecagon flux, doubles all Majorana bands, and the mirrors exclude a chiral phase in any uniform field, so only a sublattice-staggered three-spin term drives the non-Abelian Ising phase. Beyond the Kitaev state, we find a critical semi-Dirac spin liquid, with mean-field correlations $\propto r^{-3}$ along three directions and $r^{-6}$ otherwise, and extended Dirac phases with up to $48$ fermion flavors, among them an $N_f=12$ state whose PSG forbids every singlet mass. Out-of-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya couplings gap the Dirac states of its $U(1)$ class into a mean-field spinon counterpart of the Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall insulator, with spin Chern number $1$ or $3$ and spin-carrying monopoles. Chiral states imply Kalmeyer-Laughlin, semion$\times$semion, and three-fermion orders, rotation-breaking ones show $q\to -q$ asymmetric neutron spectra, and sign-alternating fluxes break time reversal alone. Masses and monopoles in these many-flavor phases and the energetics of frustrated SHD Heisenberg models are natural next steps.
summary:
- Classifies fermionic parton mean‑field states on the square‑hexagon‑dodecagon lattice via projective symmetry groups, linking its $Z_2$ PSGs to the $p6mm$ lattice with time reversal.
- Identifies an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid with a single $Z_2$ PSG, Majorana band doubling from dodecagon flux, and a non‑Abelian Ising phase driven

title: Transport Signatures of a Kinetically Self-Trapped Nagaoka Polaron
abstract: arXiv:2610.23013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nagaoka polarons are canonical examples of kinetic magnetism. Although their spin structure is well understood, their transport remains unexplored. We compute the dynamical mobility of a single hole in the square-lattice $t$-model using resummation-based quantum Monte Carlo and analytic continuation. Upon cooling, an incoherent Drude-like response gives way to a finite-frequency peak as the dc mobility vanishes. The peak signals an internal mode of a hole confined by its ferromagnetic cloud. Our results establish transport as an incisive probe of polaron formation and kinetic self-trapping.
summary:
- Calculated dynamical mobility of a single hole in the square‑lattice $t$‑model via resummation‑based QMC and analytic continuation.
- Found a crossover from incoherent Drude‑like response to a finite‑frequency peak as temperature lowers, indicating vanishing dc mobility.
- Identified the peak as an internal mode of a hole confined by its ferromagnetic cloud, demonstrating transport as a probe of kinetic self‑trapping.

title: Crystal Field-Phonon Coupling in ErFeO$_3$ Single Crystal Via Inelastic Neutron Scattering
authors: Guochu Deng, Xiaoxuan Ma, Wanting Yang, Wei Ren, Shixun Cao, Zhenxiang Cheng, Garry J. McIntyre
abstract: arXiv:2610.23015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal-field (CF) excitations and their coupling to lattice vibrations were investigated in ErFeO$_3$ using inelastic neutron scattering. Pronounced modifications of the excitation spectra, including energy shifts, intensity redistribution, and linewidth changes, were observed as a consequence of CF-phonon coupling. Significant renormalization of the first and second CF excitations, located near 5 meV and 12 meV, respectively, was detected along both transverse and longitudinal directions in the vicinity of the reciprocal-space point Q = (2, 0, 4). The coupling effects become more prominent as the temperature increases from 300 K to 650 K, while a slight suppression is observed at 750 K. Remarkably, CF excitation peaks that are strongly weakened by thermal population effects re-emerge in specific momentum regions through interaction with phonon modes. The coupled excitations exhibit characteristic signatures of hybridization, including energy renormalization, intensity enhancement, and linewidth narrowing. Density-functional-theory-based phonon calculations further support the interpretation of CF-phonon coupling in ErFeO3. These results demonstrate that strong interactions between CF excitations and lattice vibrations can substantially modify the excitation spectra in rare-earth orthoferrites.
summary:
- CF excitations (~5 meV, 12 meV) hybridize with phonons, shifting energies, redistributing intensity, and narrowing linewidths.
- Coupling strengthens from 300 K to 650 K, then slightly weakens at 750 K; thermally suppressed CF peaks re‑emerge through phonon interaction at specific Q.
- DFT phonon calculations confirm the CF‑phonon coupling, underscoring its major influence on the excitation spectra of rare‑earth orthoferrites.
